sections.title: Your focus
sections.intro: This assessment helps us understand where you are today across six pillars of longevity: Nutrition, Sleep, Movement, Mind, Connection and Prevention. There are no right or wrong answers. You tell us what you'd like to improve, and your answers show us where the greatest opportunity is. Your Good Span comes from both, and we'll explain why each practice is in it. It takes about 15 minutes.

sections.title: About you
sections.intro: These questions help us suggest practices that are safe and suitable for you.

sections.title: Prevention
sections.intro: Everyday choices that protect your health over time. There are no right or wrong answers, and your answers are private.

sections.title: Your life and your practices
sections.intro: Last few questions. These set the limits your Good Span will respect.

questions.text: Which one or two areas would you most like to improve?
questions.hint: Select up to 2. We'll still ask about every area. Your Good Span may also include practices from other areas where your answers show the greatest opportunity. We'll always explain why.
options: Nutrition - how you eat and your everyday food habits
Sleep - your sleep and sleep routines
Movement - your physical activity and movement
Mind - your mental and emotional wellbeing
Connection - your relationships and social connections
Prevention - everyday choices that protect your health over time, such as alcohol, smoking, check-ups and sun protection

questions.text: What is your age?
Which best describes your working pattern?
Has a doctor or other healthcare professional ever told you that you have any of these?
options: Diabetes (including if you take insulin or other blood-sugar medicine)
A lung condition, such as asthma or COPD

questions.text: In the past 3 months, have you experienced any of the following?
options: Pain, tightness or pressure in your chest
Shortness of breath with very little effort
Your heart racing, fluttering or beating irregularly
Pain in your calves when walking

questions.text: Did any of these happen during or just after physical activity?
Have you talked to a doctor about them?
options: Yes, and they're happy for me to be more active
Yes, but I haven't been told it's OK to be more active yet

questions.text: Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?
How does your eating pattern typically look?
rows: Vegetables and fruit on a typical day
Main meals that include a source of protein
Home-cooked main meals in a typical week
Whole grains, such as oats, wholegrain bread or brown rice
Sugary drinks, such as soft drinks, energy drinks or sweetened coffee or tea
Packaged or processed foods, such as ready meals, packaged snacks or processed meats
Adding salt to your food, at the table or when cooking

questions.text: How often do you do these at meals?
rows: Pay attention to the taste and smell of my food
Eat slowly, putting my fork down between bites
Eat a wide variety of plant foods
Have a plan for eating well when I'm out or travelling
Eat within a set daily time window

questions.text: What would you most like to improve about how you eat?
options: Heart health: less salt and more nuts
Eating well when I'm out or travelling
When I eat, such as late-evening eating
Eating more mindfully, with fewer distractions

questions.text: Are there any health, dietary or other considerations we should take into account?
options: Dietary restriction or preference (for example vegetarian, vegan, halal or kosher)
A health condition that affects what or how I eat

questions.text: On a typical night, how many hours of actual sleep do you get?
Which of these happen to you on 3 or more nights a week?
options: It takes me a long time to fall asleep
I wake during the night and find it hard to get back to sleep
I wake earlier than I want to and can't get back to sleep

questions.text: Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing while you sleep?
When do you usually have your last drink containing caffeine?
questions.hint: Include coffee, tea, cola and energy drinks.

questions.text: How long before bed do you usually finish eating?
Which of these sleep habits do you have now, and which have you tried?
cols: I've tried it, but it didn't help
rows: Get outside in daylight in the morning
Dim the lights in the evening
Keep a regular bedtime and wake time
Cut down on alcohol in the evening
Follow a relaxing wind-down routine, such as breathing, relaxation or calm music
Write down tomorrow's tasks before bed
Keep my bedroom quiet, for example with earplugs
Avoid screens in the 30 minutes before bed
Keep my phone out of bed
Work with a professional or a sleep programme such as CBT-I
Share sleep goals or progress with others

questions.text: Which aspects of your sleep would you most like to improve?
options: Waking at the time I want
Having a more consistent sleep schedule

questions.text: Which of these currently affect your sleep?
On average, how many days a week do you do moderate or vigorous exercise, such as a brisk walk, that makes you breathe harder?
On those days, on average, how many minutes do you exercise at this level?
On how many days a week do you do strength or resistance exercise, such as weights, bodyweight exercises or resistance bands?
On a typical day, how many hours do you spend sitting, including at work, travelling and watching TV?
If you track your steps, roughly how many do you take on a typical day?
Which of these do you already do regularly?
options: Short bursts of vigorous activity, such as taking stairs fast
Exercise with others or in a group
Walk or cycle to get places

questions.text: Where do you usually do your movement or exercise?
What would you most like to improve?
Is there anything we should take into account when suggesting movement or exercise?
options: A fall in the past 12 months
A health condition that affects movement or exercise

questions.text: How much time a week do you spend in green spaces or nature, such as parks, woodland, gardens or beaches?
On a typical day, how much time do you spend on social media?

questions.hint: These four questions help us suggest practices that suit how you're feeling right now. They are not a diagnosis.
questions.text: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following?
rows: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Little interest or pleasure in doing things

questions.text: What would you most like to improve in this area?
options: Spending less time on my phone or social media

questions.text: Which of these are currently part of your routine?
options: Time for hobbies or enjoyable activities
Working towards goals that matter to me
Tools for building habits, such as if-then plans
Creative hobbies, such as drawing, crafts or playing an instrument

questions.text: In a typical month, how often do you…
rows: Talk to friends or family by phone or video
Meet friends or family in person
Take part in a group, club or class

questions.text: Which of these do you already do in a typical week?
options: Do small acts of kindness for others
Tell people what I appreciate about them
Respond with enthusiasm when others share good news
Ask follow-up questions and really listen
Share how I’m really feeling with someone I trust
Get in touch with people I haven’t seen for a while
Chat with people I don’t know well, such as neighbours
Cook or share food traditions with others
Hug or share affection with people close to me

questions.text: What, if anything, would you like from your connections with other people?
options: More time with friends or family
Staying in touch with people who live far away
Helping others or contributing to my community

questions.text: Do you currently smoke or vape?
cols: I used to, but I've stopped
rows: Cigarettes, cigars, rolling tobacco or other tobacco

questions.text: Would you like to stop smoking or vaping?
Have you tried to stop smoking or vaping before?

questions.hint: One drink means a small beer (250 ml), a small glass of wine (100 ml) or a single measure of spirits (30 ml).
questions.text: How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?
On a typical day when you drink, how many drinks do you have?
How often do you have 6 or more drinks on one occasion?
When did you last have your blood pressure checked?
Which of these apply to you?
options: I've been sunburnt, or used a sunbed, in the past 12 months
I often find it hard to follow conversations, or ask people to repeat themselves

questions.text: How often do you learn something new or practise a mentally challenging hobby, such as a language, an instrument or a craft?
What would you most like to improve in this area?
options: Taking only the supplements I need
Protecting my skin from the sun
Breathing cleaner air at home and outdoors
Keeping my mind active by learning new things

questions.text: Is there one personal habit or practice you'd particularly like to work on during your Good Span that we haven't covered?
questions.hint: Optional. Something you'd like to start, strengthen, reduce or stop. It could be health-related or more personal: drinking less, reading again, learning a language, using your phone less, calling family more often, stopping smoking or volunteering.
options: Keep this private in my Journal
Share this with my Pilot so they can support me

questions.text: Which of these do you enjoy?
questions.hint: Select all that apply. We'll use this to suggest practices you're more likely to enjoy.

questions.text: The Good Span asks for about 45-60 minutes a week. How much time could you realistically give to your practices in a typical week?
questions.hint: Your Good Span will never ask for more new time than this. Things you already do don't count.

questions.text: How big a change feels right for you to start with?
options: Small, easy steps. I'm not sure how much I can manage right now
I'm ready for a bigger challenge

questions.text: Are there any types of practice you'd rather not do?
options: Tracking or counting what I eat
Using apps or devices to track things
Practices involving physical affection or touch
